summary: Audited all 71 JSON files in deploy/data (plus the 512-monument, 16-tour-stop, tutorial, timeline and road datasets embedded in bundle.pretty.js) with 18 scripts. Headline results. (1) Placements are 1,804 rows, not the 430,000 the schema promises; only 188 of 675 ticks (27.9%) have any row and 0.75% of displayed unit-ticks are real data. The renderer never interpolates across keyframe gaps and never clears its last-position cache, so 92% of transitions are hold-then-snap (371 snaps >500 m, 84 >2 km) and 404 of 478 units are stale by 100+ ticks at tick 675. (2) 95 of 478 placed unit IDs (216 rows) do not exist in the OOB; 10 Confederate regiments are keyed U- and render as Union; 28 IDs denote two different formations (e.g. U-V-3-1 McCandless vs 'Vincent's brigade'). (3) Casualty figures have no authority: Union 22,803/23,138/23,049/23,055 and Confederate 23,125/23,025/28,000/23,231 (published totals checked via Wikipedia's citation of Busey & Martin and the OR, not the book); '51,000' mixes bases; casualty_apportionment.json is not used by the animation; 22/22 Union and 9/9 Confederate divisions and 10 of 11 corps do not roll up; VI Corps has 36 regiments but no brigade records. (4) Dashboard C7 root cause is a nested notable_intensity_notes shape, and its claim is contradicted by the site's own OOB. (5) The Historian reads e.title/e.description that do not exist, so 137/137 chronology answers print 'undefined'; the indexed corpus is 11,088 words of a 45,096-word data lake. (6) 467 is regiment records only (103 batteries extra; only 217 regiments and 41 batteries ever have a position); 445+ = 467-22. (7) 1,591 user-facing ' -- ', internal IDs and dev notes in text, 0 per-record provenance, two divergent monument datasets, deep-link params that no code reads. The report contains 30 fix specs (DI-01..DI-30), a 60-rule validator spec with today's baselines, a facts-registry plan, versioning/changelog and provenance schemas, corpus statistics, a 95-row ID crosswalk seed and phasing.

findings.title: Dense, validated unit-movement model: replace 1,804 sparse rows and hold-and-snap rendering with authored anchors plus generated per-tick tracks
findings.evidence: Only 188/675 ticks have any row; 487 have none (s03_ticks.py). y1 blends only tick f and f+1 (bundle.pretty.js:96266-96305) and the cache i2 is never cleared (:96265): 1,116 of 1,209 transitions are hold-then-snap, 371 snaps >500 m, 84 >2 km, 704 km total; median implied moving speed 0.27 mph; 0.75% of displayed unit-ticks are real data; 404/478 units stale >=100 ticks at t675; 173 units have one keyframe; 59 of 73 tick-1 rows share 7 identical longitudes (schematic).
findings.root_cause: Positions authored as a few hand-written keyframes per unit with no pathing, presence windows or lookup contract; schema promises 600-700 units per tick.
findings.fix: Authoring format data-src/tracks/<day>.json with presence{appear_tick,depart_tick,off_map_until} and anchors[{tick,lat,lng,bearing,disposition,basis,source,uncertainty_m}]. build-tracks.mjs densifies each anchor pair along the road graph (Dijkstra, per-disposition speed caps: march 3 mph, double-quick 4.5 for <=4 ticks, charge 8 for <=2 ticks, retreat 6, cavalry 12/5, limbered artillery 4) or great-circle with easing; build FAILS if caps cannot be met and names the extra anchors needed. Targets: moving gap <=6 ticks, stationary <=45; historian reviews only the 162 segments >60 ticks. Ship anchors + polylines (<600 KB raw/<120 KB br) with one shared trackAt(unit,tick,frac) ES module used by map, Compare, Camera, Ledger, Embed, Immersive. Renderer owner replaces y1/i2 with trackAt and deletes the global cache.
findings.acceptance_test: Validator C001-C005 and G003 pass; 200 random (unit,tick) probes return a position for every unit whose presence covers the tick; max one-tick displacement <= cap x 5 min except <=10 whitelisted rout events; cold seek to tick 300 draws >=300 units; no unit drawn >45 ticks after its last anchor unless presence says so; Day-2 screen recording shows 0 jumps >250 m.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Core function (B/D -> A), Historical/data consistency, Usability
findings.correction: Evidence reproduced exactly (y1 at bundle.pretty.js:96266, i2 at :96265 never reset). Corrections: (1) speed caps and gap targets assume 5 min/tick but DI-11 adopts a 0.8-42.3 min/tick clock; under that clock segments >8 mph rise 2->6 and >4 mph 16->33 (C-I-3-3 t550->551 = 12.9 mph), so G003/C002 must use clockAt-derived dt. (2) Densifier timing policy (arrive-on-time vs depart-early) is unspecified. (3) 'Historian reviews only 162 segments' is optimistic: ~4,737 generated intermediate anchors vs 1,687 real rows, plus 173 single-keyframe and 153 Day-1-only units needing presence research; 8-10 d covers tooling only. (4) Consumer list wrong: Living Ledger and Embed read no placements; camera, cinematic-export, compare, ground-remembers, immersive, regiment, sandbox, watch-together, unit-rendering-reference read only placements_* (694 rows), never density_*. (5) Renderer change is a patch to the minified bundle (N1). (6) 0.27 mph median is over all non-zero segments; 0.46 mph for segments >250 m.

findings.title: Canonical unit-ID namespace, explicit side field, alias crosswalk and collision resolution
findings.evidence: 95 of 478 placed IDs unresolved (216 rows, 12.0%); 10 Confederate regiments keyed U- (U-15AL,U-44AL,U-48AL,U-1TX,U-4TX,U-5TX,U-11NC,U-26NC,U-47NC,U-52NC) render blue because side = startsWith('U-') (bundle.pretty.js:96484,96525,96585,96597,96679,96739,97068,97923) while C- twins are also placed; 28 IDs (44 rows) used for two formations, e.g. U-V-3-1 McCandless vs 'Vincent's brigade', U-II-3-1 975 vs 12,500 men, C-III-2-1 Pettigrew vs 'Archer's brigade'; second numbering scheme in density files (C-II-4, C-III-4-x, C-I-5-x, U-I-2-3/2-4); Follow-Ancestor list built from placement IDs (bundle.pretty.js:101026-101039) prints 95 raw IDs.
findings.root_cause: Two authoring passes with different ID conventions; side encoded only in the prefix; no referential validation.
findings.fix: Define ID grammar per unit_level (R007) and add side and unit_level to every OOB record and track; ban startsWith('U-') in code. Create unit_aliases.json seeded from crosswalk_seed.csv (95 rows: 12 high auto-apply, 17 medium + 44 low need short human review, 22 need new OOB records such as VI Corps brigades, C-CAV group, U-ART-RES). Migration script rewrites IDs everywhere, merges twins by (unit,tick), logs to CHANGELOG. Resolve the 28 semantic collisions row by row using semantic_id_conflicts.csv (Vincent->U-V-1-3, Webb->U-II-2-2, Archer->C-III-2-3, Gordon->C-II-1-3, Hoke/Avery->C-II-1-2, Ramseur->C-II-3-4). Give parent formations their own group/division records.
findings.acceptance_test: Validator R001-R007 and R011 report 0 errors across placements, density, chronology units_involved, vignette units_featured, succession unit_id; 0 rows where side != prefix; Follow-Ancestor list has 0 raw-ID rows and sorts numerically by sort_key (unit test on 217-regiment roster).
findings.correction: Counts reproduced (728 OOB IDs, 478 placed, 95 unresolved, 216 rows, 10 side-prefix errors with placed C- twins). startsWith('U-') side inference is at 19 bundle sites, not 8 (also :98875,99767,100906,101034,101134,101734,102336,102673,103129,103258,103320) plus static pages (search.html:110, historian.html:91, find-ancestor.html:115, regiment.html:165,194). The 28-ID/44-row collision list is a heuristic: about half are genuine brigade swaps, the rest are level errors or a cameo false positive (C-I-3 'Longstreet's corps'). The t55 rows C-II-1-1/-1-3/-1-4 rotate each other's identities, so migration must be an atomic permutation. Proposed targets (Vincent->U-V-1-3, Webb->U-II-2-2, Archer->C-III-2-3, Gordon->C-II-1-3, Hoke/Avery->C-II-1-2, Ramseur->C-II-3-4, Cutler->U-I-1-2) verified against OOB. Crosswalk seed has errors (see missed item on U-8IL etc.).

findings.title: One authority for casualty and strength numbers; derive every roll-up
findings.evidence: Union 22,803 (corps totals) / 23,138 (dashboard period sum) / 23,049 (OR, OOB army) / 23,055 (B&M via Wikipedia); Confederate 23,125 / 23,025 / 28,000 (OOB army) / 23,231 (B&M p.260); Confederate corps strength 65,000 (OOB) vs 72,810 (apportionment) vs 71,699 (B&M engaged) vs 75,000; U-I periods +335 vs total, C-CAV -100; 22/22 Union and 9/9 Confederate divisions and 10/11 corps do not sum from children; 17 of 88 brigades >10% off their regiments; '51,000' in Help chunk, chronology t650, V-001, V-024 = 23,049+28,000; casualty_apportionment.json:227 Pickett ~2,700 > C-I day-3 total 2,614:222; Confederate 37.3% divides 28,000 by campaign-start 75,000.
findings.root_cause: Hand-typed numbers from different sources and bases; no parent==children rule.
findings.fix: authorities.json with each aggregate, basis, source and alternates (B&M 23,055/23,231, engaged 93,921/71,699, OR 23,049, AG 23,003) - verify against the book before publishing. Choose one headline (e.g. ~46,300, older estimates to 51,000) and replace all '51,000' occurrences. Derive regiment->brigade->division->corps->army sums at build; keep reported_* beside derived_* and an explicit unlisted_* remainder. Fix U-I and C-CAV period sums, pick one Confederate strength basis, add killed/wounded/captured per side. Retire typed notable_intensity_notes.
findings.acceptance_test: N005-N007 pass; Dashboard totals == sum of regiments == headline (+/-0.5%, remainder shown); grep for '51,000' returns 0; Help, Dashboard, Ledger, OOB, Documentary display identical totals (E2E string test); percentages use same denominator type.
findings.correction: All aggregates reproduced (22,803/23,138/23,049; 23,125/23,025/28,000; 90,164/72,810/65,000; U-I +335; C-CAV -100; Pickett 2,700 vs 2,614 at casualty_apportionment.json:227/:222) and Wikipedia wikitext confirms 23,055/23,231/93,921/71,699/23,003/75,000/28,000 and '46,000 and 51,000'. Corrections: literal '51,000' occurs 6 times (helpmodal 1, chronology_day3 1, vignettes_part1 2, vignettes_part3 2), not 8 (8 only with two '28,000' literals). Wikipedia attributes B&M's 23,231 to the 2005 work while every site file cites B&M 1994 - edition must be reconciled before adopting 23,055/23,231 as the headline.

findings.title: Fix Dashboard stat-card contract (highest_single_regiment_rate) and compute all notable stats
findings.evidence: casualty_apportionment.json:330-333 holds {union:{unit,rate,note},confederate:{...}}; dashboard.html:244-247 pushes num: n.unit || key, note: n.note -> 'highest_single_regiment_rate' / undefined. Note text says '224 of 262 casualties' (it is 224 casualties of 262 engaged); claim 'highest Confederate rate C-26NC 69.7%' is contradicted by OOB (C-8VA 148/193=76.7%, C-38NC-S 75.6%, C-9VA 75.5%); developer footnote at dashboard.html:257-262.
findings.root_cause: Polymorphic schema, typed facts, renderer assuming one shape.
findings.fix: Replace object with array notable_intensity[{id,label,side,unit_id,display_name,value,value_label,note}] generated at build from the OOB with a stated rule (min 150 engaged): Union U-1MN 85.5% (224 of 262 engaged), Confederate top by rate per rule plus separate 'most casualties' card C-26NC (588 of 843 engaged); notes templated from numbers; dashboard skips cards missing label/note and never prints a key; remove the reconcile footnote after DI-03.
findings.acceptance_test: No card text contains '_' or 'undefined'; test asserts card count and note regex '\d+ casualties of \d+ engaged'; values equal a recomputation from OOB.
findings.correction: Root cause exact (casualty_apportionment.json:330-333; dashboard.html:244-247; footnote :257-262). C-8VA 148/193=76.7%, C-38NC-S 75.6%, C-9VA 75.5%, C-26NC 69.7%, U-1MN 224/262=85.5% reproduced (same ranking without the 'min 150' rule, so it is unnecessary). The hotfix (flatten nested union/confederate objects, fix '224 of 262 casualties' wording) is S with no build; the OOB-generated notable_intensity array requires the not-yet-existing build/validator (DI-24/25), so that version is M and 'Depends: none' is wrong for it.

findings.title: Repair the Historian/data contract: chronology 'undefined', lost paragraphs, unindexed entity kinds
findings.evidence: historian.html:119,123 read e.title/e.description but chronology rows have event/narrative: 137/137 answers render 'undefined' and are indexed by location only (419 words); :109 prints 7,182 script words as one string; terrain limited to 30 key_locations (:130); brigades, batteries, successions, monuments, tour stops, army/corps records not indexed; probe queries Meade, Longstreet, Lincoln, Jennie Wade, 'Who commanded the Union army?', 'How many casualties...' return nothing relevant (s07_historian_sim.js).
findings.root_cause: Each page re-implements field parsing; no shared corpus contract or tests.
findings.fix:
(a) Quick fix: use e.event/e.narrative/e.significance, index event+narrative+location, render full_script.split('\n\n') as

, add roads/structures/features. (b) Shared assets/corpus.js reading a documented corpus.json built at deploy (used by historian, search, find-ancestor, regiment) with kinds army/corps/division/brigade/battery/succession/monument/tour/fact. (c) Golden set of 40 queries asserting expected ID in top 3.
findings.acceptance_test: 0 answers contain 'undefined'; precision@3 >=0.8 on the golden set; answers render as paragraphs; K001 passes.
findings.correction: historian.html:119,123 confirmed; chronology keys are event/narrative, 137/137 render 'undefined' (rerun; port verified literal vs historian.html:154-190). Addendum: fixes (a)/(b) alone will not reach P@3>=0.8 because the ranker outranks the correct record even for the site's own chips: '20th Maine' -> U-20ME rank 4, '1st Minnesota' -> U-1MN rank 4, 'Little Round Top' -> LOC-003 rank 26. Golden set needs a title/entity boost or BM25 in the same item.

findings.title: Deep-link and share-link contract: 521+ generated links land on tick 1
findings.evidence: search.html:114,127,139 generate ?unit=, ?tick=&vignette=, ?lat=&lng=; historian.html:110 generates /?tick=&vignette=; bundle.pretty.js:97823-97829 writes ?t=&u=&z=&ll=; the only param the app reads is ancestor (bundle.pretty.js:101019). regiment.html:252 and embed.html:41 read their own params.
findings.root_cause: No shared URL grammar; links generated from data are never validated against a reader.
findings.fix: routes.json defining ?t,u,v,ll,z,a,day with legacy aliases; shared parseDeepLink()/buildDeepLink(); app applies state on load; validator R008 resolves every generated link (unit has a track, tick 1-675, vignette exists); regiments without a track link to regiment.html?unit= until DI-19.
findings.acceptance_test: Playwright opens each of 521 search results and asserts tick/unit/vignette state; share-link copy-reload round trip restores tick, zoom, center, selection; R008 = 0.
findings.correction: Only 'ancestor' is read (bundle :101019); writers search.html:114,127,139, historian.html:110, bookmarks :97822-97829 confirmed across bundle, all assets/*.js, index.html and site-nav.js. Add embed.html's CTA (?tick=&vignette=, unread) to the writer list.

findings.title: Complete the OOB hierarchy (VI Corps) and make it add up
findings.evidence: 36 regiments reference 8 non-existent U-VI-*-* brigades; division.brigade_ids dangling for 8; 8 placement rows use those IDs; union_oob_brigades.json note says 49 infantry brigades but has 43 infantry + 8 cavalry (43+8 missing VI = 51); regiment->brigade: strength equal in 9 of 88, >10% off in 17; guns Confederate sum 182 vs 'approximately 283', Union 278+28=306 vs 'approximately 370'.
findings.root_cause: Hand-authored levels never reconciled; no reciprocal-link validation.
findings.fix: Add the 8 VI Corps brigade records (commanders, strengths, casualties from OR/B&M - names not researched here); fix metadata note; make parent_brigade_id resolve and regiment_ids reciprocal (431/467 today); derive artillery totals from batteries; add army records U-AOP and C-ANV with derived totals; introduce unlisted_* remainders.
findings.acceptance_test: R003/R004 = 0; N005/N006 pass or carry documented remainders; N010 guns equal sum of gun_count.
findings.correction: VI Corps facts reproduced (36 regiments -> 8 missing brigades; 51 = 43 infantry + 8 cavalry; note says 49). Corrections: 28/28 divisions with resolvable brigade children fail to roll up (19 Union + 9 Confederate); the '22/22 Union' includes 3 VI Corps divisions whose children do not exist. Guns: derived Confederate total is 194, not 182 (3 horse batteries/12 guns in confederate_cavalry.json), and published totals (Wikipedia infobox ~360 Union / ~270 Confederate) far exceed the OOB's listed batteries (55 Union/306 guns; 48 Confederate/194), so 'derive totals and reword 283/370' would under-state; complete the artillery OOB first.

findings.title: Aliases, duplicates, detachments, misfiled rows and 'Commander unrecorded' leaking into Search/Historian
findings.evidence: U-14BK '14th Brooklyn (alias for U-84NY)' strength 0 ranks #1 for '14th brooklyn' (90 vs 60); U-11PA (Paul's brigade) and U-11PA-B 'Baxter detachment' (fate 'See U-11PA') duplicate one regiment; U-107NY in I Corps likely the 107th PA; 4 Union cavalry -b detachments; C-McClanahan-ART (a battery) in a regiments array; 27 rows 'Commander unrecorded' (search.html:112) and 222 rows ending in dangling ' · '; 29 rows with alias/detachment/battalion markers.
findings.root_cause: No record_type/visibility model; alias implemented as a row.
findings.fix: Add record_type, alias_for, visibility; aliases become aliases[] on the target; merge true duplicates (U-11PA-B into U-11PA, strength per B&M); move McClanahan to horse_artillery; group detachments under parent; commander null -> 'Commander not recorded in Busey & Martin', fill 22 Confederate cavalry commanders or set commander_status:unknown; compute casualty_percentage; search meta joins non-empty parts only.
findings.acceptance_test: Search '14th brooklyn' returns the real regiment first and 0 alias rows; 0 rows containing 'unrecorded' or dangling ' · '; R006 = 0.
findings.correction: U-14BK scores 90 vs 60 for the real 84th NY on '14th brooklyn' (search.html:83-95 + record check). Merge caution: the 11th PA historically belonged to Baxter's brigade (verify vs B&M), so the U-I-2-1 (Paul's) U-11PA record is likely the misfiled one; merge direction must keep the Baxter's-brigade parent. C-McClanahan-ART has explicit unit_type 'horse_artillery' (arm is not merely inferred).

findings.title: Single-source-of-truth facts registry for every count and label
findings.evidence: '467' appears 10 times (index.html:15,18,24,32,719,754; manifest.json:4; find-ancestor.html:48,105; historian.html:48); '445+' in helpmodal chunk (=467-22); '24 vignettes/137 events/30 terrain' in historian.html:48; '51,000' 8 times; index.html:721-740 lists 18 features vs 20 in site-nav.js; disposition colours differ between schema and Lp (bundle.pretty.js:96307); speed label '1x (real time)' at :97429.
findings.root_cause: Numbers typed into prose in >14 places.
findings.fix: Build emits facts.json (derived counts + cited authorities) and injects {{facts.*}} into HTML, JSON-LD, manifest, Help/About, PDF build and Historian intro; features.json generates both nav and SEO block; dispositions.json generates schema enum, legend, colours; facts:lint bans literals generated from facts values.
findings.acceptance_test: facts:lint finds 0 literal registry values outside facts.json; changing a record count updates every surface after rebuild; Help About and home meta description show the same number.
findings.correction: 467 x10, 445+, 18 vs 20 links and '1x (real time)' :97429 reproduced; '51,000' is 6 literals not 8. The sample facts.json lists minutes_per_tick:5 beside clock.json (piecewise, 0.8-42.3 min/tick) - contradictory. Templating HTML/JSON-LD needs a build step; dependency line omits DI-24/25 (netlify.toml publish='.', no build today).

findings.title: Placement strength becomes computed from casualties instead of hand-typed
findings.evidence: 121 strength increases across 82 units (U-II-3-1 975->12,500; U-VI-1 7,500->15,000; U-CAV-1 3,200->8,000; C-III-3-1 1,734->6,300, all ID collisions); 126 units with >10% OOB casualties never change strength; 74 units exceed OOB strength by >2%; only 88 of 302 end within 5% of strength-casualties; the animation ignores casualty_apportionment.json (no fetch in bundle).
findings.root_cause: Strength typed per keyframe; apportionment model never wired to the renderer.
findings.fix: Drop strength from authored anchors; compute strength(t)=initial - cumulative casualties from one documented distribution model (DI-21) weighted by Charging/Chaotic ticks; reinforcements as explicit sourced events; parent aggregates = sum of children; validator N001-N004.
findings.acceptance_test: Every unit ends within 1% of OOB strength-casualties; every unit with OOB casualties shows >0 at the end; Dashboard corps curves equal sum of unit curves at every tick.
findings.correction: 121 increases/82 units and 74 over-OOB reproduced. '88 of 302' holds only for regiments+brigades (unstated scope; 105/374 across all levels). '126 units with >10% casualties and constant strength' is misleading: 93 of the 126 have one keyframe; only 33 have >=2 keyframes with constant strength, so the stat mostly restates DI-01. Renderer coupling omitted: F4 interpolates strength (:96238-96256) and uF (:97033-97044) triggers the casualty flash from strength drops.

findings.title: One tick-to-clock function in data; remove hand-typed times
findings.evidence: 94 of 137 chronology labels differ from their own tick_formula (t12 '6:00am' vs 5:55); succession approx_time vs approx_tick off by mean +5.07 h (0/37 within 30 min); schema day real_time strings contradict 5 min x 225 ticks; V-023 'That night' at tick 556 (same tick as V-019); TO marker tick 17 'First shot' vs V-001 tick 12; 11 of 24 vignettes contradict their tick clock; getTickTime bundle.pretty.js:9371 uses 6:00 base on Day 1 and 4:00 on Days 2-3.
findings.root_cause: Several independent clock implementations and hand-typed labels.
findings.fix: Adopt the 33-anchor clock.json from time-facts-anchors.csv as the only clockAt(tick) (ISO-8601 -04:00, date, day, label); delete typed time strings; store real_time per event and validate within 30 min (T001/T002); regex-check narrative times (T003); fix 4 wrong-day and 12 misordered events, V-023's tick and TO/Gc markers via events.json (DI-16).
findings.acceptance_test: T001-T004 = 0; grep proves a single clock formula across map, Compare, Camera, Ledger, Documentary, Sandbox; Day-3 header never shows 'July 5'.
findings.correction: 94/137 label-vs-formula mismatches reproduced, but only 46 exceed the plan's own 30-min tolerance (42 >60 min); 36 are <=5 min rounding and 11 <=15 min. getTickTime :9371 (6:00/4:00 bases) and 'July ${l + 2}' :97428 confirmed. TO marker (:112192) 'First shot' at tick 17: chronology t17 is Calef's first UNION artillery fire and tutorial Gc t17 is 'First Artillery Fire' - the label is wrong, not the tick. Adopting the piecewise clock makes 'five-minute snapshots' copy false and the alternative (re-tick all data to a linear clock) is not weighed.

findings.title: Machine-enforced JSON Schemas replace prose placement_schema.json
findings.evidence: Schema claims 430,000 records (actual 1,804), 600-700 units per tick (max 87), 4 day-1 files (3 exist plus 38 undocumented density files), record_count 4,890 (actual 100 at placements_day1_ticks1_50.json:7), declared tick ranges wrong (101-225 actual 120-225; 601-675 actual 620-675), day real_time strings inconsistent; not JSON Schema; 12 KB shipped unused; lat/lng range excludes approach corridors (49 rows).
findings.root_cause: Documentation written as prose and never enforced.
findings.fix: JSON Schema 2020-12 under schemas/ (unit, regiment, battery, brigade, track, event, vignette, terrain, source) with additionalProperties:false and enums; docs to docs/data-model.md; stop deploying the schema; headers build-derived; replace bbox with map_extent + off_map flag.
findings.acceptance_test: ajv validates every file; unknown key fails build; schema not deployed.
findings.correction: placement_schema.json:5,12,13 (430,000+, 600-700); placements_day1_ticks1_50.json:7 record_count 4890 vs 100; 49 rows outside bbox (42 lng<-77.29, 7 lat>39.85); 379 rows <4 decimals; schema unused (only a comment at compare.html:121).

findings.title: Geometry: map extent, East Cavalry Field, precision, stacking, terrain duplicates, road geometry
findings.evidence: 49 rows outside schema bbox; 26 monuments east of -77.18 and cavalry placements 2.7-3.0 km west of the site's own ECF tablets (V-020 trigger 2.5 km off); 379 rows with <4 decimals; 48 stacked groups (96 units); LOC-023 is 26 m from LOC-001 and four location/structure pairs share coordinates; 'Gulp's Hill saddle'; terrain roads have one point each while the bundle hard-codes straight road lines (bundle.pretty.js:9450).
findings.root_cause: No geometry validation or shared road/land layers.
findings.fix: Widen map_extent to ~-77.15; relocate ECF anchors from the tablet cluster (historian check) and update LOC-021/V-020; require >=5 decimals or uncertainty_m>=50; enforce 15 m min separation with auto-nudge for the 48 groups; merge duplicate terrain entries and fix spellings; single roads.geojson used by routing and map layer.
findings.acceptance_test: S005/G001/G002/G004 = 0; ECF anchors within 300 m of tablet centroid; one roads file feeds routing and map.
findings.correction: ECF offset reproduced (tablet centroid 39.8282,-77.1677 is 2.5 km from LOC-021; t560-565 cavalry rows 2.6-3.1 km west). Stacked units: 48/96 on raw rows, 39/78 after last-writer-wins. Missed renderer coupling: main map maxBounds (:97244) already includes ECF but the minimap hard-codes Wa lat 39.77-39.855, lng -77.28..-77.185 (:99664), so widening map_extent in data alone leaves ECF/approach units off the minimap.

findings.title: Duplicate and conflicting (unit_id,tick) rows; deterministic precedence
findings.evidence: 103 duplicated keys / 117 redundant rows; 68 keys conflict (C-III-3-2 t120: Line of Battle 1,326 vs Charging Line 1,100 about 1.3 km apart); app loads placements then density (bundle.pretty.js:96900-96915) and y1 is last-writer-wins. See dup_conflicts.csv.
findings.root_cause: Two overlapping authoring layers merged by load order.
findings.fix: Merge density into authoring tracks (one row per unit,tick); until then document precedence and make S007 fail on conflicting duplicates; resolve the 68 by hand (mostly ID collisions).
findings.correction: 103 keys/117 rows/68 conflicts reproduced; load order at zp :96900 and addPlacementsForDay :9397 confirmed. The interim rule 'density > placements' holds only on the map; eight static pages read only placements_*, so they display the losing row.

findings.title: Monuments: one dataset with provenance, moved out of the JS bundle
findings.evidence: data/monuments.json has 9 records (overlay index.html:640-700, fetch :677) while a different 512-record array is embedded at bundle.pretty.js:104440-110609 (~121 KB as JSON): 503/512 src empty, 51 blank mn, duplicate MN 96, #512 honors text corrupted ('(WGS-84 decimal degrees). findings.title: OOB-to-map coverage: every regiment and battery has a position when present
findings.evidence: 250 of 467 regiments (53.5%) have no own placement (231 drawn only via parent brigade; 19 have neither); 62 of 103 batteries never placed; home meta claims '467 regiments and batteries tracked across 675 snapshots'; only 217 regiments can be followed in the ancestor list.
findings.root_cause: Brigade-level authoring with no derived regimental layout.
findings.fix: Formation model deriving regiments along the brigade line by OOB order and strength-based frontage (schema's 0.045 yd/man gives 77 m for 1,883 men vs about 520 m for two ranks at ~0.55 m per file - verify with a drill manual), batteries beside battalion anchors; mark as reconstructed/approximate in UI.
findings.acceptance_test: Every OOB unit whose presence covers a tick has a position at that tick; Follow-Ancestor lists 467 regiments and 103 batteries; home-page claim becomes true.
findings.correction: 217 own / 250 not / 231 via parent / 19 neither reproduced. Batteries never placed are 65 of 103, not 62 (the report's own s02 table has 33+5=38 placed). Frontage arithmetic checks (77 m vs 518 m) but the 22-in/file figure still needs a drill-manual cite.

findings.title: Text lint and typographic normalisation pipeline
findings.evidence: 1,591 ' -- ' in user-facing fields (839 placement notes, 353 key_action, 119 vignette script); 72 strings with internal IDs (US-001, CS-011) plus 'CS-017' in a placement note; 60 flag_notes dev strings; typos Krzyznowski (x1 vs Krzyzanowski x10), Nichols's (x1 vs Nicholls x10), 'Gulp's Hill saddle', 'Brian Farm (Bryan Farm)', Rose Woods 19 vs Rose's Woods 4; 249 paragraph breaks collapsed by innerHTML.

findings.fix: Strip authoring fields at build; typographic normaliser (' -- ' -> em dash, curly quotes); lexicon.json gazetteer with Levenshtein-1 near-miss report; banned-token rules; style guide; paragraphs[] arrays.
findings.acceptance_test: X001-X005 = 0 on published output; canonical spellings everywhere.
findings.correction: Typo counts reproduced (Krzyznowski 1/Krzyzanowski 10, Nichols's 1/Nicholls 10, Gulp's 1, Brian Farm 1, Rose Woods 19/Rose's Woods 4). ' -- ' count is scope-dependent: 1,799 in non-metadata strings, 1,938 raw; the report's 1,591 is a defensible subset.

findings.title: One casualty-timeline algorithm generated once
findings.evidence: Dashboard uses a piecewise 70%-at-peak curve (dashboard.html:98-118), Living Ledger a linear ramp (living-ledger.html:102-118), JSON documents sigma=8/4 bell curves (casualty_apportionment.json:10-11), animation uses none; Ledger shows 4 casualties at tick 1 because U-CAV period starts at tick 1 while the first shot is tick 12.

findings.fix: Build emits casualty_timeline.json (per side/corps/tick, K/W/C) from the DI-10 model; Dashboard, Ledger, Compare, Documentary and heat-map read it; day-1 periods start at first documented engagement.
findings.acceptance_test: Sum of unit casualties at tick t == Ledger == Dashboard at 20 sampled ticks; Ledger starts at 0.
findings.correction: Linear ramp (living-ledger.html:102-118) and tick-1 count 290/74=3.9 confirmed. The same loop has an off-by-one (see missed item: Ledger totals overshoot by +412 Union / +426 Confederate).

findings.title: Per-record provenance, source registry and confidence
findings.evidence: 0/467 regiments, 0/1,804 placements, 0/137 events, 0/24 vignettes have per-record sources; only 42 successions (page-level cites) and 9 of 512 monuments do; 54 of 71 files lack metadata.sources; 29 distinct citations with no pages or editions; schema claims 5-10 m accuracy for coordinates that are rounded (379 rows) or schematic (59/73 tick-1 rows).

findings.title: Repository, data versioning, changelog and public errata page

findings.title: Package 71 data files into a few immutable packs and strip authoring bytes
findings.evidence: 71 files, 824,704 B (160,243 B gzip-9); code issues >=34 JSON requests at load (14 OOB + terrain + 3 vignettes + 16 Day-1 files, bundle.pretty.js:96754-96935) plus 3 chronology fetches (:102958-102960) and a duplicate commander_successions fetch (:97522); ~18 KB dev-only keys, 35 KB metadata and 12 KB schema ship to users; 512-monument array inside JS.
findings.root_cause: Authoring layout deployed as-is.
findings.fix: Emit core, day1-3, history, monuments and corpus packs with content hashes; strip flag, flag_notes, chunk, metadata; immutable caching; prefetch Day 2 at idle; SW precache by data_version.
findings.acceptance_test: <=4 data requests before first paint; first-paint data <=80 KB brotli; total data <=400 KB brotli; RUM LCP/INP not worse.
findings.correction: 71 files/824,704 B reproduced, but '160,243 B gzip-9' is a concatenated-archive figure; real per-file transfer is 199,009 B gzip-9 / 161,679 B brotli-11. Today's first-load set (34 requests) is ~95.5 KB brotli, so budgets of <=80 KB first paint / <=400 KB total are 16% below today and 2.5x above today's entire data; data is not the LCP bottleneck (JS is). Loader already lazy-loads Day 2/3 (:96943-96946) and swallows fetch failures (:96909), so renamed/hashed files fail silently; file lists (eF/tF/nF :96754-96831) live in the bundle and nine static pages. /data/ max-age=3600 with a never-expiring network-first SW cache already causes up to 1 h code/data skew.

findings.title: Historian knowledge-base data contract and corpus expansion (data side)
findings.evidence: Corpus today: 658 indexed entries / 11,088 indexed words / 45,096 narrative words in the whole data lake (regiment key_action 3,380, vignettes ~8,781, chronology 4,791, placement notes 12,081, monuments 6,915, tour 2,031, brigades 3,107, batteries 2,186); 698 distinct commander names, 85 chronology locations, 50 terrain entries, 512 monuments, 42 successions, 29 cited sources unindexed.
findings.root_cause: Corpus is what happened to be in the JSON; no entity/passage model or sourcing pipeline.
findings.fix: JSONL kb/ with entity types person, unit, place, event, monument, source, passage; passage={id,text<=220 words,entity_ids,ticks|date_range,place_ids,source_id,locator,license,confidence}; stable IDs; numeric answers rebuilt from structured tables; Phase 1 limited to public-domain/permitted sources (OR Vol. 27 reports, one report summary per brigade ~300 passages, monument texts subject to NPS/HMDB terms, ~300 person bios, ~50 place essays) plus a 300-question gold set.
findings.acceptance_test: Corpus >=10x current words with 100% sourced passages; gold-set P@3 >=0.85; 0 unsupported claims in a 100-answer human audit; every answer shows source links.
findings.correction: Word counts re-derived within 3% (tokenisation differences). Licensing: OR Vol. 27 public domain is sound; 'NPS/HMDB terms' is unverifiable (HMDB 403); ~300 person bios have no named source (Wikipedia would be CC BY-SA share-alike); Stone Sentinels has no stated licence. 10x corpus = ~110k words/~650 passages; XL plausible only if bios/place essays are authored in-house.

open_questions: Does the site have rights or permission to republish Busey & Martin per-regiment strength/casualty tables (467 rows), or should only aggregates and original prose be published? (licensing not verified)

Which casualty headline should the site use: Busey & Martin 23,055 + 23,231, or OR-era 23,049 + about 28,000? The plan assumes B&M with a stated range; reference totals were verified only through Wikipedia's citation, not the book.
Should the map extent be widened east (about -77.15) and East Cavalry Field re-located, and is there a trusted local source for tablet coordinates?
Is 'approximate regiment positions inside the brigade line', labelled as reconstructed, acceptable, or must only documented positions be shown?
Should '14th Brooklyn' be exposed as a search alias of the 84th NY rather than a row (recommended)?
Are OR (public domain), NPS and the owner's own prose the only permitted corpus sources for Historian Phase 1?
Can the owner supply Busey & Martin / OR access to fill the 8 missing VI Corps brigades and 22 Confederate cavalry commanders, or should Phase 1 mark them unknown?
Confirm no other authoring copy of the data exists; the plan treats deploy/data as canonical.
verification_summary: Nothing was refuted. I re-derived the report's headline numbers from scratch against DEPLOY_DIR/data, bundle.pretty.js, live curl and an independently fetched Wikipedia wikitext, and they reproduced exactly. That covers 188/675 ticks populated, 1,116 of 1,209 transitions snapping, 95 unresolved IDs, 10 U- Confederates, 103 duplicate keys, the 137/137 chronology "undefined", 512 monuments and the VI Corps gap. The cited bundle line numbers also hold. The report has three kinds of problem. (1) Cross-finding inconsistencies it did not notice. The main one is that DI-01, DI-09 and DI-10 assume 5 minutes per tick, while DI-11 adopts a 33-anchor clock running 0.8 to 42.3 minutes per tick. Under that clock, segments faster than 8 mph rise from 2 to 6. (2) Fixes that quietly depend on editing the source-less minified bundle (N1) and on nine static pages that hard-code the placements_* filenames and never read density_*. (3) A few overstated or mis-scoped statistics: 126 "constant-strength" units (93 have only one keyframe), 94 clock mismatches (only 46 exceed 30 minutes), 51,000 x8 (actually 6), 62 unplaced batteries (65), and the 160 KB gzip figure (a solid-archive number). I appended a "## Verification" section with the full verdict table and 8 missed issues to data-integrity.md. Scripts are in plan-work/tmp-verify-data-integrity/. Licence statements for HMDB and NPS are UNVERIFIABLE: HMDB returned 403, and Stone Sentinels shows a copyright notice but no reuse licence.

missed_by_specialist.title: Plan is inconsistent on the clock: 5 min/tick constants vs the piecewise clock DI-11 adopts
missed_by_specialist.evidence: DI-01 acceptance ('<= speed cap x 5 min'), DI-09 facts.json ('minutes_per_tick': 5 beside 'clock': 'clock.json@1.0.0'), DI-10/21 and site copy ('675 five-minute snapshots', index.html:15,18,24,32,719,754, manifest.json:4, schema 'The 5-minute tick number') assume 5 min/tick, but time-facts-anchors.csv runs 0.8-42.3 min/tick (ticks 302-314: 0.8; 515-518: 42.3). Recomputed implied speeds under that clock (tmp-verify-data-integrity/v01c.py): 6 segments >8 mph and 33 >4 mph vs 2 and 16 on the linear clock (C-I-3-3 t550->551 12.9 mph).
missed_by_specialist.fix: Owner decision before DI-01/10/21: (A) keep the warped clock, rename to '675 moments', derive every speed/gap/percent from clockAt; or (B) re-tick all placements/events/vignettes/successions/markers onto a linear 5-minute clock via a monotone remap tick'=f^-1(real_time), keeping 'five-minute' and the mph math.
